wine_name: Plantagenet Omrah Pinot Noir, Great Southern
wrong_facts: Omrah is described as 'their premium Pinot Noir expression' when ground truth confirms it is actually the second-label/value range
Claims indigenous yeasts and whole-bunch fermentation with no supporting data — these are fabricated winemaking details
Fabricated price range of $45-60 AUD — no pricing data was provided and Omrah as a second label would likely be much cheaper
Claims sourcing from 'select blocks within Mount Barker and Frankland River sub-regions' — ground truth says Omrah uses younger vineyards or bought-in fruit
Ancient granite soils in the hook — while Great Southern has some granite, the ground truth specifies gravelly loam soils for Plantagenet's vineyards
Aging potential of 15 years is implausible for a second-label Pinot Noir that received only bronze medals
Yarra Yering Dry Red No. 1 is not a Pinot Noir competitor — it's a Bordeaux blend
reasoning: The most damaging error is calling Omrah a 'premium Pinot Noir expression' when ground truth confirms it's the second/value label — this fundamentally misrepresents the wine's market position and appears in the wine_summary. Multiple winemaking details (indigenous yeasts, whole-bunch fermentation) are fabricated with no basis in context or ground truth. The $45-60 AUD price is fabricated and likely too high for a value-tier label. The comparison to Yarra Yering Dry Red No. 1 is misleading since that's a Cabernet-based blend. The voice is decent — direct and opinionated — but built on a foundation of incorrect claims. Hard penalty applied for fabricated numbers.
